subject: HBIO
title: Human Biology – Form 4
source: Form 4 scheme of work, 3 h/week; dates approximate, worked out from the sequence and week numbers

chapters.title: Supply of man's needs in animal and plant resources

lessons.title: 1. Introduction to Human Biology: characteristics of man as a mammal; man as a unique mammal; structure and function of man
2.1–2.4 Nutrition in plants: nutritional requirements, photosynthesis and its significance
2.5–2.7 The green leaf as an organ of photosynthesis; factors affecting the rate; experiments
2.8 Fate of translocated food (use, excretion, storage of food reserves)
2.9 Fungi: nutrition, growth, reproduction and useful fungi (mushroom cultivation)

chapters.title: Module 1: The living world – nutrition in man

lessons.title: 3.1–3.3 Classes of food and their sources; deficiency effects; chemical composition of carbohydrates, proteins and lipids
3.3 Food tests (practical)
3.4–3.6 Balanced diet; enzymes and their characteristics; role of enzymes in digestion
3.7–3.8 The alimentary canal: structure and adaptive functions; fate of the products of digestion
4. Digestive disorders (obesity, constipation, indigestion, diarrhoea, heartburn, hernia); hygiene of the mouth and teeth

chapters.title: Module 2: Health education – invasion of the environment by pathogenic micro-organisms

lessons.title: 5. Viruses and emerging diseases: structure and replication; HIV/AIDS; Ebola
6. Prevention of infections: terminology; behavioural, physical and chemical barriers; serum and vaccine therapy; other viral diseases
7. Bacteria: characteristics, structure and reproduction; bacterial diseases (cholera, typhoid, diphtheria, tetanus, tuberculosis)
8. The immune responses: specific and non-specific; natural and artificial, active and passive immunity; the lymphatic system

chapters.title: Module 2: Health education – physical, social and community health

lessons.title: 9. Physical and social health: exercise, rest and sleep; effects of alcohol, smoking and drugs
10.1–10.3 Community health: health centres and clinics; types of hospitals; roles of hospital units and medical officers
10.4–10.6 Geriatric homes; playgrounds and gymnasia; charitable and social organisations
10.7–10.8 Personal hygiene: care of head and hair, mouth and teeth, eyes and ears, hands and feet, skin and genitals
11.1–11.5 The circulatory system: heart and blood vessels, blood cells, tissue fluid and lymph, heart beat and blood pressure
11.6–11.12 Pulmonary and systemic circulation; capillary exchange; blood tests; hygiene, accidents and diseases of the cardiovascular system
12. Gaseous exchange and respiration: lungs, breathing, internal respiration; hygiene and respiratory infections
13.1–13.5 The urinary system: organs, urine formation, water-salt balance, diseases, prevention and treatment
13.6–13.11 The skin and its hygiene and diseases; the liver and its disorders
14.1–14.4 The skeletal and muscular systems: functions, bones, joints and movement

chapters.title: Module 2: Health education – skeleton and muscles (continued)

lessons.title: 14.5–14.8 Postures and deformities; fractures and sprains; feeding and exercise for bones
14.9–14.12 Muscles: types and functions, cramp and oxygen debt, spasms and injuries, muscle diseases

chapters.title: Module 3: Environmental education – managing nutritional relationships in ecosystems

lessons.title: 15. Saprotrophic nutrition: role of saprotrophs; bread mould; nitrogen fixation; decomposition of sewage and refuse
16. Parasitism: types; life cycles of roundworms, flatworms and protozoa; parasitic food chains
17.1–17.2 Conservation of biodiversity: interdependence of living organisms
17.3–17.8 Legislation on poaching, fishing and forestry; man and the environment; greenhouse effect and climate change; the ozone layer; natural disasters in Cameroon
